source.title: Composable Interventions for Language Models
source.authors: Arinbjörn Kolbeinsson; Kyle O'Brien; Tian-Jin Huang; Shanghua Gao; Shi-Wei Liu; J. Schwarz; Anurag Vaidya; Faisal Mahmood; M. Zitnik; Tian-Long Chen; Thomas Hartvigsen

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures WMDP performance after applying quantization to models unlearned with GA, GD, or RMU. This directly tests whether quantization changes access to targeted knowledge, though the study frames the experiments as intervention composability rather than as an explicit recovery attack.
record.gate_note: Relevant results are the WMDP measurements for unlearning followed by quantization in Table 18. The paper does not test recovery by relearning, activation ablation, or prompting. Its other editing, compression, and composability results do not bear on those claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study is not designed as a recovery attack. It is a composability study, but its unlearning→compression tables report WMDP accuracy after GPTQ/AWQ quantization of GA-, GD- and RMU-unlearned Llama3-8B (Table 18), which bears on D. Its unlearning→editing table reports WMDP after fine-tuning-based edits on unrelated zsRE facts (Table 21), which bears on B.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that compression hinders unlearning (mainly when compression comes first), that order matters, and that unlearning should precede compression. They also say editing does not disrupt forgetting (excluding GA), which Table 21's GD→LoRA 0.54 contradicts, because their order-free metric takes the better order. They do not frame any result as knowledge recovery.
record.recipe_differences: The study composes GA, GD, and RMU with GPTQ and AWQ compression and measures WMDP; it does not design or optimize quantization as a recovery attack.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with unlearning method, quantizer, bit-width, and intervention order. The paper reports that GA has poor unlearning performance, while GD and RMU perform better.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning applied to an already-quantized or pruned model forgets less (e.g. GPTQ 4-bit→RMU WMDP 0.45 vs RMU alone 0.29).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compression before unlearning reduces unlearning effectiveness.

fits_no_version.finding: Pruning after RMU does not raise WMDP (RMU→SparseGPT/Wanda 0.25–0.29).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pruning of unlearned weights does not restore forgotten knowledge.

record.problems: WMDP is acknowledged by the authors as an imperfect evaluation of unlearning writ large. The quantization results are for Llama3-8B and a limited set of methods and bit-widths; GA does not provide a near-chance unlearning baseline. Uncertainty is not given alongside the specific Table 18 values.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant unlearning-recovery rows were omitted. The paper's other compositions, editing metrics, MMLU results, and unlearning→pruning results do not directly test version D's quantization condition.

untested.parts: The study reports RMU and GD unlearning reaching near chance with MMLU retained, but tests no deliberate attacks.
Only incidental fine-tuning via knowledge edits on 50 unrelated zsRE facts. No relearning on forgotten-set subsets or loosely related data, and no attack designed for recovery.
No activation-direction ablation or access-vs-deletion analysis.
Only Llama3-8B and only GPTQ/AWQ. No other quantizers (e.g. round-to-nearest) or models for unlearning→quantization.

missing.what: Unlearning→editing WMDP: GD→LoRA 0.54, GD→FT 0.29, GD→MEMIT 0.28, RMU→FT 0.32, RMU→MEMIT 0.30, RMU→LoRA 0.29, GA→FT/MEMIT/LoRA 0.47/0.45/0.34. Fine-tuning on unrelated data bears on B.
Higher-bit quantization after unlearning: RMU→GPTQ 8-bit 0.29; RMU→AWQ 5/6/8-bit 0.28/0.28/0.29; GD→GPTQ 8-bit 0.24 (MMLU 0.35); GA→GPTQ 8-bit 0.45.
MMLU and WikiText PPL for each unlearning→quantization condition, needed to see that GD/GA and 2-bit rows reflect model collapse.

record.verdict_notes: GD's quantized variants have MMLU ~0.27–0.35 and PPL inf or astronomically large, so GD×quantization WMDP values near 0.24 are collapse, not deeper forgetting. The reader's 'reversed' states for these rows are wrong. The GD→LoRA WMDP jump (0.26→0.54) after editing 50 unrelated zsRE facts is an unflagged relearning-style recovery, though it comes from a single setting without reported variance.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures unlearning performance and MMLU, but does not test whether simple recovery attacks fail.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning attack intended to recover forgotten knowledge is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access-blocking versus deletion is tested.
Tests GPTQ and AWQ quantization at 2, 3, and 4 bits after GA, GD, or RMU on Llama3-8B; does not test other quantizers or models for this recovery question.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context recovery attack is tested.
No newer method is evaluated for resistance to the specified recovery attacks.

relation.reason: Table 18 and Table 21 report WMDP after quantization or editing of unlearned models, which bears on versions D and B.

tranche.reason: This is a composability study, not designed as a recovery attack. It reports WMDP after quantizing (Table 18) and editing (Table 21) unlearned Llama3-8B, which is a new setting with a result on the claim. The reader's T2 fits less well.

source_check.notes: Tables 15/18/21 are extracted column-wise; I placed the rows by position and checked them. GA alone only partly forgets (WMDP 0.46, MMLU 0.50, PPL inf), which weakens the GA rows. Not in the checked rows: GD→AWQ 3-bit rises 0.26→0.33, but the model is collapsed (MMLU 0.33, PPL inf). GD→Wanda 0.45 reaches WMDP 0.46 (pruning, not version D). The l2 group mixes MEMIT (not fine-tuning) with FT/LoRA.

statements.correction: Llama3-8B, avg WMDP (Tables 15, 18): GA→None 0.46, MMLU 0.50, PPL inf. GA→GPTQ 4-bit 0.43, MMLU 0.48. GA→GPTQ 2-bit 0.25, MMLU 0.25. GD→None 0.26, MMLU 0.52, PPL 4.48. GD→GPTQ 2-bit 0.24, MMLU 0.27, PPL inf. GPTQ 2-bit→None 0.25, MMLU 0.24.
statements.problem: The prose never names this study, and its conditions (MUSE, 8/4-bit) leave out Llama3-8B, WMDP and 2-bit. Of the cited rows, D07 is GD (retain-constrained, MMLU 0.52 unquantized), and D01/D07 are 2-bit, where quantization alone collapses even the base model. GA-only keeps MMLU 0.50.

statements.correction: Table 18: 2- and 3-bit GPTQ and AWQ after each of GA, GD and RMU on Llama3-8B, measured on WMDP/MMLU/WikiText PPL. No MUSE/TOFU.
statements.problem: The six named rows are not the study's only sub-4-bit results. Table 18 also reports GA→GPTQ 3-bit, GA→AWQ 3-bit, GD→AWQ 2/3-bit and RMU→GPTQ/AWQ 2-bit. It is right that all sub-4-bit results are WMDP-only on Llama3-8B.
